The central type a plugin author fills in has 20 public fields and not one is documented, including four that only accept fixed vocabularies enforced with ValueError (`section` core/data/models/results/toxo, `stage` alpha/beta/stable, `kind` assay/importer/analysis/utility, `call_style` settings/folder) — none of which appear anywhere in the published docs.

The class is a frozen dataclass holding `key` plus a `"module:callable"` reference *string*, not a callable — the summary describes the function the record points at, so a reader arrives expecting to call the contribution object.

The enumeration is presented as exhaustive (the module docstring even says "these are exact"), but `cmd_run` propagates a pipeline's own `SystemExit` code verbatim (`code = exc.code if isinstance(exc.code, int) else EXIT_RUNTIME`), so any integer a module exits with reaches the shell.

The `checks` parameter — the documented-in-the-module-header way to run a subset of checks, and the reason each check is independently callable — is not mentioned at all, and the summary's "every check" contradicts its existence.

Like `ModelProviderContribution`, this describes the referenced builder rather than the class, which is an immutable record of `key`/`title`/`builder`/`after` — and `after` ("statistics") is the one field a plugin author must actually decide about, with no explanation of what values are valid.
